Prescription
Effective power what the eye receives through the lens as tilted +6.00DS
Compensated power to order order this and the tilted lens delivers the dialled Rx +6.00DS
Martin's rule. Tilting a lens through θ about its horizontal meridian acts on the sphere component of the Rx as written. The sphere becomes Fs = F(1 + sin²θ ⁄ 2n), and the cylinder it induces, Fc = Fs·tan²θ, lands at axis 180 and adds to whatever cylinder the lens already carried. To compensate, divide the desired sphere by that same multiplier and subtract F·tan²θ from the desired cylinder. Vertex distance plays no part in any of these numbers — Martin's rule has no vertex term, and the 13.5 mm gap drawn here only positions the eye in the picture. Index is the one material property that matters and is set by the dial above. Because the rule works on the sphere as written, transposing the same lens to the other cylinder form changes the answer slightly; dial the Rx the way it is written. The defocus drawn inside the eye is enlarged ×5 so the foci visibly leave the fovea.
